approach: Seed the CLDR punctuation tier and a base-produced group into the existing phase-B draft store through addProposed/addWithProvenance, computing the groups and the ASCII fallback floor in a pure engine module beside convenienceChars. Add an always-rendering 'invisibles' spine step between punctuation and convenience that owns format-character decisions in a sticky store record and emits the same phase-C confirmedInventory union as the punctuation step. Story 4's rejection ledger already exists (spec 044 FR-017); the draft-restore path that drops it on reload is fixed as its own commit.

decisions.decision: Both phase-C inventory emitters (PunctuationStep, InvisiblesStep) emit the same NFC-deduped union via phaseCConfirmedInventory(), so recordPhase field-wise merge never clobbers
decisions.why: recordPhase shallow-merges same-phase results; a second confirmedInventory emitter would overwrite the first; mergePhaseResults unions across phases so accepted invisibles reach the session inventory without a contracts change
decisions.rejected: New optional SurveyPhaseResult field (contracts change, would not reach confirmedInventory); reporting under phase D (misuses phase vocabulary)

decisions.decision: Reuse the existing rejected[] ledger and fix draftPersistence.applyEnvelopeToStores to forward all sticky snapshot fields, as a separate fix commit
decisions.why: phaseBDraftStore already implements the rejection veto (spec 044 FR-017); the only gap is that restore forwards only chars/exemplarDigraphs/selectedFont and wipes rejected/provenance/etc. on reload; that is a pre-existing defect blocking Story 4
decisions.rejected: A new RejectionLedger entity as the pre-plan data model proposed

decisions.decision: Pure engine module punctuationProposal.ts owns ASCII_PUNCTUATION_FLOOR, basePunctuationCoverage(ir) and buildPunctuationProposal(); hasUnaccountedOpaqueFragment exported from computeInventoryDelta.ts
decisions.why: Mirrors convenienceChars.ts precedent (pure, colocated test, barrel export); SC-001 becomes a per-tag function oracle over the offline index; one derivation of coverageComplete
decisions.rejected: Taking an InventoryDelta as input (needs a needed list; base group is the produced side); placing helpers in packages/contracts (shapes only, cannot import engine)

decisions.decision: DraftProvenance stays single-valued (gains base, ascii-floor); multi-source attribution derived at render from the proposal groups
decisions.why: provenance map is read by chips, setAll, snapshot and spec-044 tests; an array would touch all of them for a presentational need

decisions.decision: Format characters entered on the punctuation page are handed off (acceptInvisible + status note), not navigated; carry-over migrates Cf chars out of the draft controls bucket into invisibleDecisions
decisions.why: Forced navigation breaks typing flow and walk order; leaving carried-over chars in chars would duplicate them into the alphabet answer and the new step answer (FR-017)
decisions.rejected: Keep the Skipped path; navigate immediately; adopt without removing from chars

decisions.decision: Retire pb_rtl_direction_marks + pb_rtl_direction_marks_detail (rewire pb_rtl_short_vowels.next), registry count 114 to 112
decisions.why: FR-019 subsume-not-duplicate; no studio code consumes the detail answer; dead modules still extract catalog keys
decisions.rejected: Gate the modules off with an always-false condition

decisions.decision: Both steps declare inputs: [] and writes: [] (resolves the spec open decision)
decisions.why: spec 066 FR-006 explicit-empty rule; confirming an inventory is a survey result not an IR write; an input with no upstream writer fails the orphan-input check; convenience precedent
decisions.rejected: Declaring base-coverage reads as IRPath inputs

decisions.decision: {"decision": "The studio seeds only the Unicode-punctuation members of the ASCII floor (23 of 32); the engine constant stays the full 32-character FR-007 definition", "why": "The punctuation page collects and emits glyphCategory === punctuation only; the nine symbol members ($ + < = > ^ ` | ~) would land in the unrendered symbols bucket and reach the alphabet result unseen (FR-025). Symbols are family default 5, out of scope and shielded by carve anyway", "rejected": "Shrinking ASCII_PUNCTUATION_FLOOR to 23 (breaks the contract invariant and FR-007 ranges); widening the page to accept \p{S} (would let typed $ into a page that declines it today)"}
The base group is seeded only when a working copy IR exists; a null IR proposes nothing, and the ASCII floor is reserved for a base whose output is UNKNOWABLE (opaque fragments)
decisions.why: In the app a working copy always exists by the punctuation step; seeding 23 floor chips into every IR-less render (tests, degraded states) would misreport a missing base as an unknowable one (FR-008)
decisions.rejected: Treating baseCoverage === null as incomplete coverage in the studio and seeding the floor

decisions.decision: Ticking a suggestion the author previously removed is an author add (provenance author), not a proposal add
decisions.why: addProposed is vetoed by the rejection ledger, so the re-tick would silently do nothing; ticking back is as deliberate as typing (FR-022 override). Never-rejected ticks keep proposal provenance so the existing attribution test holds
decisions.rejected: Clearing the rejection and re-adding as a proposal (would re-propose on the next seed)

decisions.decision: The golden-walk harness mocks sourcedExemplars to null
decisions.why: On a warm exemplar index the punctuation step seeds the locale tier before the walk clicks Done; unplaced typographic marks then block the Phase F coverage gate whose <dialog> jsdom cannot showModal(). That is the product working as specified (FR-011), not a traversal fact the oracle records; PunctuationStep.test.tsx owns seeding
decisions.rejected: Installing the dialog shim (the gate would still block the walk short of done); resetting the draft store between walks (would not fix the warm-index case)

decisions.decision: writingDirectionFrom precedence: Phase A writing_direction, then any pb_rtl_direction_confirm answer (either value) or pb_non_roman_branch === rtl, then surveyContext.script_family/routing_group, else unknown
decisions.why: pb_rtl_direction_confirm is only asked on the RTL branch, so its presence is the signal; script_family rtl is the identity prefill; every other family is LTR
decisions.rejected: Adding a direction field to the draft store

decisions.decision: A format character typed with other text (e.g. a + ZWNJ) is declined as a mixed cluster, not split
decisions.why: Intl.Segmenter treats ZWJ/ZWNJ as grapheme extenders, so the typed unit really is one cluster; splitting would invent characters the author did not type (FR-021)
decisions.rejected: Splitting the cluster into its code points
